scalesUsed.notes: E - F# - G - A - B - C - D - E
scalesUsed.application: Shapes the dark, heavy four-chord foundation (i - bIII - bVI - bVII) of the verses and chorus

scalesUsed.notes: E - G - A - Bb - B - D - E
scalesUsed.application: Powers Jimi Hocking and Grant Walmsley's searing unison bends and iconic intro riff

keyAndScale.modalCharacter: Gritty Newcastle hard-rock Aeolian aggression charged with high-octane pub-rock anthemic hooks
keyAndScale.relativeMinor: E minor is the relative minor of G major

mainProgression.description: The quintessential minor-key rock anthem progression: grounding the tonic in Em, lifting through G and C, before hammering the D dominant substitute back home.

sectionProgressions.description: Crushing full-gain power chord sprint with ringing unison bends and stadium roar
Palm-muted low-E chugging building steady tension beneath Dave Gleeson's gritty vocal narrative
Major IV chord lift injecting sudden Dorian swagger before plunging back into the chorus

harmonicFunction: Em (i) - Heavy minor tonic anchoring the dark, rebellious rock attitude
G (♭III) - Relative major chord providing an explosive momentary burst of light
C (♭VI) - Submediant chord adding poignant emotional weight to the progression
D (♭VII) - Subtonic chord providing powerful modal drive and resolution back to Em
A (IV) - Dorian major subdominant introducing swagger and contrast in the bridge

techniques.name: Palm-Muted Heavy Power Chording & Unison Bends
techniques.description: Tight right-hand palm muting on the lower strings contrasted with wide screaming unison bends at frets 12 and 15

sequence: Rest the heel of the picking hand lightly across the bridge saddles
Chug steady eighth notes on the low E string with aggressive downstrokes
Open up into wide, ringing power chords on the chord changes
Execute whole-step unison bends on strings 2 and 3 at the end of each riff cycle
tips: Keep high gain tight by pulling back the amp bass slightly and pushing midrange to 7
Support your ring finger with middle and index fingers when pushing unison bends
Hit the crash cymbal hits in unison with the drummer on beat 1

techniques.name: Crybaby Wah Pedal Sweeps & Searing Unison Bends
techniques.description: Aggressive vocal-like wah-wah filter sweeps paired with high-gain whole-step unison bends and rapid pentatonic blues bursts

notes: Rock the wah heel-to-toe in sync with whole-step bends at the 14th and 15th frets
Unison bends: fret 12 high E while bending fret 15 B string up a full step
Climb to fret 17 on the high E string for the solo climax
sequence: Engage the wah pedal at the start of the solo break with a toe-down bite
Sweep from heel (dark low-mid vocal) to toe (screaming treble bite) on sustained bends
Execute rapid alternate-picked blues cascades down the E minor pentatonic box
tips: Keep your heel grounded and rock from the ankle to avoid losing rhythm balance
Push the amp's midrange to prevent the wah from disappearing into the drum crash cymbals
Mute adjacent unplayed strings with your fret-hand index finger to prevent unwanted squeals

sections.name: Intro Crushing Power Riff
sections.technique: Palm-Muted Heavy Power Chording & Unison Bends
sections.description: Screaming opening guitar riff and chugging power chords that define 90s Australian pub rock.
notes: Heavy palm-muting on the low E pedal note with aggressive downstrokes
Punch the G5 and C5 accents with authoritative downstroke attack
Let the D chord ring before cycling back into the main riff

sections.name: Verse 1 Palm-Muted Chug
sections.description: Dave Gleeson begins the narrative ('I am the king of the castle...') over locked-in eighth-note chugs with tight heel muting.
notes: Clean eighth-note palm muting across the lower strings
Keep the pick close to the strings for minimal wasted motion and maximum punch
Follow the bass drum kicks for an immovable pocket

sections.name: Pre-Chorus Dorian Ascent
sections.description: The song breaks from the Aeolian chug with a bold A major (IV) chord lift, injecting swagger and building tension toward the chorus.
notes: Switch from palm muting to open ringing power chords
Emphasize the C# note in the A major chord for the characteristic Dorian color
Crescendo on the D power chord to propel the band into the chorus

sections.name: Chorus Stadium Hook
sections.description: Huge singalong chorus on 'Better, better than you!' with wide-open power chords and aggressive vocal harmonizing.
notes: Lift all muting and hit full open power chords across all strings
Strike with aggressive downstrokes on beats 1, 2, 3, and 4
Let the ringing top strings fill out the sonic space

sections.name: Blistering Wah-Wah Guitar Solo
sections.technique: Crybaby Wah Pedal Sweeps & Searing Unison Bends
sections.description: Jimi Hocking / Grant Walmsley's blistering, wah-drenched guitar solo. Features aggressive Crybaby sweeps, whole-step unison bends at the 14th/15th frets, rapid 12th-fret pentatonic blues runs, and screaming 17th-fret climax bends.
notes: Engage the wah pedal with an aggressive forward sweep into the 12th-fret high E note
Execute a screaming whole-step bend on the 14th fret G string and 15th fret B string
Rip through the 12th-position E minor pentatonic box with fast alternate picking
Climb to the 17th fret of the high E string for the howling whole-step bend climax

sections.name: Outro Power Jam & Climax
sections.description: The band enters full arena overdrive, with ad-lib screams from Dave Gleeson and howling feedback, ending on a final sustained Em power chord crash.
sections.progression: Em - G - C - D (repeating to crashing stop)
notes: Keep the rhythm driving with maximum energy and downstroke punch
Toss in 15th-to-19th fret bends and wild pick slides over the repeating cycle
Conclude with a thunderous hit on the open Em chord and let the valve feedback howl

guitar.recommended: Gibson Les Paul Standard or Gibson SG (humbucker muscle)
guitar.pickup: Bridge humbucker for cutting crunch and sustain

effects.distortion: ProCo Rat or Boss SD-1 Overdrive tightening the front end
effects.other: Dunlop Cry Baby Wah for the lead solo sections

beginner.title: Open Chords & Steady Strumming
steps: Learn open Em, G, C, and D chords
Practice transitions between the four chords at 90 BPM
beginner.goals: Smooth chord changes without stopping the right hand

intermediate.title: Palm Muting & Power Chord Speed
steps: Shift to root-5 and root-6 power chords (E5, G5, C5, D5)
Master the tight palm-muted chug at 124 BPM using our Metronome
Practice shifting cleanly between frets 0, 3, 5, and 7
intermediate.goals: Crushing rhythm tone with zero unwanted string noise

advanced.title: Lead Solo & Unison Bending
steps: Learn the soaring unison bends at frets 12 and 15
Transcribe the high-energy pentatonic wah-wah solo
Incorporate pinched harmonics on the low strings
advanced.goals: High-octane pub-rock lead performance with commanding stage presence

commonMistakes: Pressing too hard with the palm on the bridge saddles, causing the pitch to go sharp
Rushing the transition from C5 to D5 in the chorus
Using too much amplifier bass which creates muddiness when chugging at high volume
practiceRoutine: Warm up with 3 minutes of palm-muted 16th-note alternate picking on the low E string
Practice the intro riff at 100, 115, and 124 BPM
Play along with the recording focusing on lock-step kick drum synchronization
focusAreas: Fast, authoritative power chord shifts up and down the neck
Intonation accuracy on 2nd and 3rd string unison bends
metronomeWork: Set click to 105 BPM and practice palm-muted downstroke chugging
Use our Metronome Speed Trainer (+3 BPM every 4 bars) up to 124 BPM
Test accuracy by muting audio click for 2 bars and coming back on beat 1
